meta.title: Otaku Japan
meta.sources: Cross-referenced from the Google Maps export: favorites and want-to-go lists, the saved places sheet, and the Otaku/Arcades/Music/Thrift + film-sites layers of the private My Maps.

akihabara.label: Neon Akihabara
akihabara.story: The district itself, before any shopping. Katsu curry at Hinoya, the FFXIV cafe in the Pasela building, the robot-staffed cafe, the owl cafe, taiyaki toward Asakusabashi, coffee at KEY'S under the tracks. When the sun drops the signage does the work, and if the night runs long, MOGRA is a basement by the tracks where the DJs play anison to people who know every word.

godzilla.label: The Godzilla Trail
godzilla.sub: Seventy years of the King, walking distance apart
godzilla.story: Its own map because it deserves one. The Wako clock tower he flattened in Minus One, the Hibiya statue that replaced the 1995 original, the Diet Building burning in Shin Godzilla, the Nakagin site on the way through Ginza. Then Kabukicho: the head over the Toho Building roars on the hour, the Godzilla Store is a block away, and Square Enix HQ sits on the east side. Out west, the statue at the gate of Toho Studios. Tokyo Tower counts too; he has wrecked it more than once.

pilgrimage.label: The Anime Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.sub: Reze arc, Jujutsu Kaisen, Shinkai, Tokyo Ghoul
pilgrimage.story: One map, several Tokyos drawn over the real one. The Reze arc is a Jinbocho afternoon: the phone booth in the rain, the cafe fans match to hers, the stone stairs where visitors leave gerbera flowers. Jujutsu Kaisen has its own blocks around Shibuya Station, Harajuku and the opening-credit spots. Suga Shrine's stairs and the Shinanomachi footbridge are Shinkai's. Tokyo Ghoul is a cafe in Kanamecho and a lunch in Ikebukuro, and Kawagoe is Tsuki ga Kirei's town.

gaming.label: Gaming & Arcades
gaming.story: The cabinet map. Super Potato's retro floors and the arcade on top, GiGO and HEY holding the Electric Town arcade line, a racing-sim shop, Mikado in Takadanobaba where the old guard still runs tournaments. Joypolis on the bay, the esports park inside Tokyo Tower, and the Dagashiya Game Museum in Itabashi for the pre-history.

shibuya.label: The Harajuku–Daikanyama Walk
shibuya.sub: Cat Street to the manga floor
shibuya.story: The walk day. Takeshita's crepe chaos into the quieter Cat Street, then south to Daikanyama T-Site: the best English manga floor in the city, Akira storyboard books in the art stacks, and Anjin upstairs with the leather chairs to read the haul. The day ends there, at dusk, on purpose.

odaiba.label: Odaiba & the Bay
odaiba.story: Take the Yurikamome over Rainbow Bridge and spend a day on the artificial island. The Unicorn Gundam transforms on schedule outside DiverCity. The miniature world of Small Worlds, then teamLab Planets at Toyosu where you wade barefoot through the art, or Borderless at Azabudai.

museums.label: The Museum Arc
museums.sub: Ghibli to Tokiwaso, the industry's memory
museums.story: The museum day out along the Chuo and Odakyu lines. The Ghibli Museum in Mitaka sells timed tickets a month ahead and is worth the planning. The Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in Koganei has the shop Ghibli drew Kamaji's drawers from, and Miyazaki's clock runs its show in Shiodome. Fujiko F Fujio's museum in Kawasaki has the original Doraemon art. Sanrio Puroland is the pink overload. Tokiwaso rebuilds the apartment where Tezuka and the Fujikos lived, and Suginami's free museum sits where the studios are. Ikebukuro's rooftop garden is the pause in the middle, and the Totoro cream puffs are in Setagaya.

yokohama.label: Yokohama
yokohama.story: Half an hour south. The Red Brick Warehouse on the harbor, Cosmoworld's wheel on the water, and Chinatown for lunch. The Ramen Museum at Shin-Yokohama doubles as the train home.

fuji.label: Fuji-Q Excursion
fuji.story: The optional detour, for a clear day. Fuji-Q has world-tier coasters and a permanent Hidden Leaf village, Ichiraku ramen included, with the mountain looming behind the Hokage faces. Coffee at Utsuwa in Gotemba on the way. Bus from Shinjuku, back in time for dinner.

nagoya.label: Ghibli Park
nagoya.story: The shinkansen west stops being transport and becomes part of the trip here. Ghibli Park sits on the old Expo grounds outside Nagoya: mostly built worlds, Kiki's bakery, Satsuki and Mei's house, the Grand Warehouse, with a carousel and the Flying Machine in the Valley of Witches. Timed entry, so this day is planned, not improvised. South of Nagoya, Nishio is matcha country: Saijoen's tea house and the Matcha Museum.

osaka.label: Osaka
osaka.story: Osaka's otaku district is Denden Town in Nipponbashi, rougher and more local than Akihabara: Animate, Jungle, figure and card shops, the Good Smile collab cafe. The FFXIV Eorzea Cafe is in Dotonbori, five minutes from the Glico sign. The castle in the morning (Godzilla wrecked it in 1955), Kuromon market for lunch, Rikuro's cheesecake, Nipponbashi until the legs give out. Kyoto is a train ride up for JOJOPUB, matcha tiramisu and Rokuyosha's doughnuts, and Kashihara in Nara has the Street Fighter statues.

usj.label: Universal Studios Japan
usj.story: The park day. Super Nintendo World is the reason: punch the blocks, ride Mario Kart, eat at Kinopio's. The anime collabs rotate through the rest of the park, One Piece and Monster Hunter among them. Express Pass buys back hours; book it early.

kobe.label: Kobe Stopover
kobe.sub: Sake town on the way south
kobe.story: The decompression stop between Osaka and the island. Kobe's Nada district is sake country: Hakutsuru's brewery museum and Shushinkan's tasting counter are twenty minutes apart on foot. Sleep by the harbor; the bridge to Awaji is tomorrow.

awaji.label: Awaji Island
awaji.sub: The island. Nijigen no Mori, Godzilla, the Kitty coast
awaji.story: The finale. Awaji is its own place: a forest park across the Akashi Kaikyo bridge where someone built the anime island. Nijigen no Mori holds the Hidden Leaf, Dragon Quest Island, and a Godzilla you zipline into. The Godzilla Museum is beside it. On the west coast, Hello Kitty Smile and Show Box face the strait, and the onion burgers at Uzunooka sit under the Naruto bridge. Stay the night on the island if you can.

return.label: The Way Home
return.story: Awaji is the far shore, so the trip home is planned. The suitcases go ahead by takkyubin courier from the island to the Tokyo hotel, so you cross the Akashi Kaikyo bridge with a day pack. The highway bus to Sannomiya takes about fifty minutes from the bridge end of the island, the Port Liner reaches Kobe Airport in eighteen, the flight to Haneda is about an hour, and the bags beat you to the room.

lastday.label: The Last Day — The Shopping Run
lastday.sub: Every store, one day, with a list
lastday.story: You never shop at the beginning of a trip. You shop at the end, with a list, and this is the list. Every store you scouted all trip, one map: the Akihabara wall of Radio Kaikan, Kotobukiya, Mandarake and Animate; Nakano Broadway's secondhand floors; Ikebukuro's flagships and the gashapon hall; Parco's sixth floor, the Harajuku vintage shops, the Gundam Base. Then Character Street for the giftable pile before the airport.

shop-akiba.label: Akihabara — figures, games, the retro wall

shop-ikebukuro.label: Ikebukuro — flagships and the gashapon hall

shop-bay.label: The bay — Gundam Base, last Gunpla stop

kissa.label: Tea, Cafes and Kawaii
kissa.sub: Tea rooms, kissaten, parfaits and lucky cats
kissa.story: The slow day. Gyokuro in three infusions at Sakurai in Aoyama, or the tea breakfast at Yakumo Saryo. Coffee at Cafe de l'Ambre in Ginza, then the goldfish at Art Aquarium and the Vampire Cafe a few blocks over. Asakusa for matcha gelato, a fruit parfait at Goto and rice-flour pancakes at Benitsuru. Gotokuji's thousand lucky cats are out west in Setagaya.

beats.title: The map is the plan
beats.text: Two weeks rebuilt out of a decade of saved pins. Tokyo first, because most of the life is there. Then the shinkansen west through Nagoya to Osaka, out to Universal, over the bridge to Awaji Island, and back to Tokyo for the last shopping day.

beats.title: Tokyo, the base
beats.text: Tokyo gets the bulk of the days, inside the Yamanote loop and out into the west suburbs. Each map below is its own world at its own scale: the districts, then the pilgrimages.

beats.title: The shinkansen west
beats.text: Bags packed, seat on the right side for the Fuji view. The Tokaido line is the oldest high-speed rail on earth and still the best way to cross the country. Nagoya for Ghibli Park, then Osaka.

beats.title: Kansai
beats.text: Osaka is a different tempo: louder, cheaper, hungrier. The otaku district is Denden Town; the castle is the morning; Dotonbori is the evening.

beats.title: The island
beats.text: Awaji is not a district of anything. It is its own place, sitting in the strait between Honshu and Shikoku, and for this trip it is the destination, not a day trip. The anime park, the Godzilla, the Kitty coast, the onions.

spots.name: AKIHABARA KOTOBUKIYA
spots.blurb: Five floors a minute from the Electric Town exit: licensed shops on 1F, Kotobukiya's own figures and kits on 2F, and an event floor on top.

spots.name: Akihabara Radio Kaikan
spots.blurb: The yellow box by the station. Ten floors: K-Books, amiami, Volks, Kaiyodo. If a hobby exists, someone in this building sells its merch.

spots.name: Mandarake Complex
spots.blurb: Eight floors of black walls and secondhand treasure. Doujin, vintage toys, cel art, cosplay. The floor guide alone is a museum of fandom.

spots.name: Animate Akihabara
spots.blurb: The mainline anime store, split across two buildings. New releases, exclusive bonuses, and seasonal pop-ups on the event floor.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田四丁目３番２号

spots.name: Akiba Cultures Zone
spots.blurb: A multi-floor otaku mall that rotates tenants. Figures, cards, idols, whatever the current wave is.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目７番６号

spots.name: Super Potato Akihabara
spots.blurb: The retro game shop: consoles and games on 3F, guides, CDs and merchandise on 4F, and a retro arcade on 5F.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目１１番２号

spots.name: GiGO Akihabara Building 3
spots.blurb: A survivor of the Sega building purge. Rhythm games, fighters and UFO catchers across several floors.

spots.name: HEY (Hirose Entertainment Yard)
spots.blurb: Taito's showcase arcade across the street. Serious fighting game floors upstairs, rows of crane games below.

spots.name: D.D.R AKIBA
spots.blurb: A racing-simulator shop. Ten minutes in a rig, automatic or manual.

spots.name: TAMASHII NATIONS STORE TOKYO
spots.blurb: Bandai's collector brand flagship. The glass cases of Soul of Chogokin and Figuarts are closer to a gallery than a store.

spots.name: COSPA Akihabara
spots.blurb: COSPA's shop, Gee!Store Akiba, on the fourth floor of the Onoden main store. Character tees, jackets and goods.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田三丁目１５番５号

spots.name: MOGRA
spots.blurb: The anison DJ bar in a basement by the tracks. DJs play anime songs and game remixes to a floor of people who know every word.
spots.matched: 東京都台東区秋葉原３番１１号

spots.name: Hinoya Curry Akihabara
spots.blurb: Katsu curry at the ticket machine: a fried cutlet over rice under dark curry. Fast and filling.

spots.name: Kyushu Jangara Akihabara
spots.blurb: Tonkotsu ramen on the main drag. The all-toppings bowl is the classic tourist move and it earns it.

spots.name: Eorzea Cafe Akihabara
spots.blurb: The Final Fantasy XIV cafe in the Pasela building. Job cocktails, moogle desserts, and dishes named after raids. Reservations recommended.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区外神田一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: Owl Cafe Tokyo
spots.blurb: A small owl cafe off the main street. Hourly slots and small groups; book ahead.

spots.name: EXBAR TOKYO plus Akihabara
spots.blurb: Taito's craft beer and game bar, opened in 2025. The Final Fantasy XIV goods shop moved in at the end of that year.

spots.name: Naruto Taiyaki Asakusabashi
spots.blurb: Taiyaki a short hop east of Akihabara. Crisp skin, red bean or custard, still warm from the iron.
spots.matched: 東京都台東区浅草橋一丁目１７番

spots.name: DAWN Avatar Robot Cafe
spots.blurb: The cafe where the servers are robots operated remotely by people who cannot easily work outside the home.

spots.name: Tokyo Character Street
spots.blurb: The underground mall on B1 of Tokyo Station's First Avenue, on the Yaesu side. About thirty character shops, Pokémon, Jump, Ghibli, Rilakkuma and Miffy among them.

spots.name: Anime Tokyo Station
spots.blurb: A small anime exhibit space inside Tokyo Station Ichibangai. Rotating displays and event corners. Free to wander.
spots.matched: 東京都千代田区丸の内一丁目９番

spots.name: Nakano Broadway
spots.blurb: The other mecca. Floors of Mandarake branches, watch shops, idol goods, Taco Che books, and Showa-era arcades.

spots.name: Mandarake Nakano
spots.blurb: Technically dozens of Mandarake micro-shops inside Broadway, each a different obsession. The anime cel and vintage toy floors are the draw.

spots.name: Nakano Sun Mall
spots.blurb: The covered arcade between the station and Broadway. Taiyaki, standing sushi, and the slow reveal of Broadway's facade at the end.

spots.name: animate Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The Animate flagship, reopened in 2023 as one of the largest anime stores in the world, with sales floors from B2 to 9F near Otome Road.

spots.name: Evangelion Store Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: Evangelion merchandise on the second floor of P'Parco in Higashi-Ikebukuro.

spots.name: Gashapon Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The world's largest capsule toy store, verified by Guinness. Thousands of machines. Bring coins and resolve.

spots.name: Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo & Pikachu Sweets
spots.blurb: The flagship Pokémon Center in Sunshine City, with Pikachu Sweets next door. The line for seasonal plush starts early.
spots.matched: Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo & Pikachu Sweets

spots.name: Animate Annex
spots.blurb: The second Ikebukuro Animate, mostly merchandise. Quieter than the flagship, same loyalty points.

spots.name: Tokiwaso Manga Museum
spots.blurb: A reconstruction of the apartment where Tezuka, Fujiko Fujio and the manga gods lived in the 50s. The birthplace of the industry, rebuilt down to the tatami.

spots.name: Dagashiya Game Museum
spots.blurb: A candy-store museum in Itabashi with playable retro cabinets and Showa junk food. Small and strange.

spots.name: A Happy Pancake Ikebukuro
spots.blurb: The souffle pancake place. Twenty minutes of jiggle per order. A good pause between stores.
spots.matched: 東京都豊島区南池袋一丁目１８番

spots.name: Ikebukuro Seibu Rooftop
spots.blurb: The department store roof garden with a Monet water-lily pond replica. The calmest square meter in Ikebukuro.
spots.matched: 東京都豊島区南池袋一丁目２８番１号

spots.name: Shibuya Parco
spots.blurb: The sixth floor is the draw: Nintendo Tokyo, Pokémon Center Shibuya, the Jump Shop and the Capcom Store, all in one strip.

spots.name: Mandarake Shibuya
spots.blurb: The Shibuya branch underground on Inokashira-dori. Smaller than Nakano but curated weird.

spots.name: Toy Sapiens
spots.blurb: Hot Toys flagship. Movie-accurate figures at movie-poster prices. Worth it just to see the craftsmanship.

spots.name: Takeshita Street
spots.blurb: The crepe-and-chaos street off Harajuku Station. In episode 3 of Jujutsu Kaisen, Yuji, Megumi and Gojo meet Nobara by the coin lockers near its entrance.

spots.name: Cat Street
spots.blurb: The quieter walk from Harajuku into Shibuya. Vintage and streetwear shops, the fashion side of the same subculture coin.

spots.name: Kinji Used Clothing Harajuku
spots.blurb: Big vintage floor under the Harajuku streetscape. Same instinct as the Koenji thrift circuit, bigger selection.

spots.name: RAGTAG Harajuku
spots.blurb: Designer resale on several floors.

spots.name: DAIKANYAMA T-SITE
spots.blurb: Where the Shibuya day ends. The Tsutaya at Daikanyama carries the best English-language manga selection in the city, and the art stacks hold storyboard books and film panels, Akira among them. Upstairs, the Anjin lounge is the reward: leather chairs, low light, a proper drink while you read what you just bought. Come at dusk, stay until closing.

spots.name: Unicorn Gundam Statue
spots.blurb: The life-size transforming Unicorn outside DiverCity. It shifts to destroy mode on a schedule with lights and the horn opening. Still the best free show on the bay.
spots.matched: 東京都江東区青海一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: The Gundam Base Tokyo
spots.blurb: The Gunpla flagship inside DiverCity 7F. Limited kits, a build space, and the most dangerous wall of boxes in Tokyo for a modeler.
spots.matched: 東京都江東区青海一丁目１番１０号

spots.name: Tokyo Joypolis
spots.blurb: Sega's indoor park at Decks. Half-pipe rides, VR coasters, the arcade floor stays loud.

spots.name: small worlds miniature museum
spots.blurb: The miniature museum in Ariake. Evangelion's Tokyo-3 in 1:80, a moving space center, an airport with departing planes. The detail level is absurd.

spots.name: teamLab Planets
spots.blurb: The barefoot digital art maze in Toyosu. Wading through knee-deep water projections. Timed tickets, sells out.

spots.name: teamLab Borderless
spots.blurb: The reborn Borderless at Azabudai Hills. Rooms that bleed into each other, no map, no wrong way.
spots.matched: teamLab Borderless: MORI Building DIGITAL ART MUSEUM

spots.name: Rainbow Bridge
spots.blurb: The Yurikamome crosses the bridge on the way to Odaiba, the cheapest bay view in Tokyo.

spots.name: RED° Tokyo Tower
spots.blurb: The esports park inside Tokyo Tower's foot building. Retro floor, VR, sim rigs. The tower itself still earns the trip up.

spots.name: Ghibli Museum
spots.blurb: The Mitaka museum. Timed tickets go on sale on the 10th of each month for the following month, through Lawson Ticket only. No photos inside. The Catbus is for children 12 and under, and the Saturn Theater short is worth the trip alone.

spots.name: Fujiko F Fujio Museum
spots.blurb: The Doraemon museum in Kawasaki. Original art and a rooftop garden.

spots.name: Sanrio Puroland
spots.blurb: The indoor Hello Kitty theme park in Tama. Fully covered, very pink, with a boat ride.
spots.matched: 東京都多摩市落合一丁目３１番地

spots.name: Suginami Animation Museum
spots.blurb: Free museum in Ogikubo covering how anime is actually made, with dubbing booths and a small theater. Suginami is where the studios are.
spots.matched: Tokyo Polytechnic University Suginami Animation Museum

spots.name: Takadanobaba Mikado
spots.blurb: The fighting game arcade that outlived everything. Tournaments, legacy cabinets, the old guard still plays here.

spots.name: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse
spots.blurb: The red-brick warehouses on the harbor, now craft beer and event halls. The bay walk here is the best in Yokohama.
spots.matched: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse (Godzilla Minus One)

spots.name: Yokohama Cosmoworld
spots.blurb: The waterfront amusement park with the clock ferris wheel. Free entry, pay per ride, open late.
spots.matched: 神奈川県横浜市中区新港二丁目８番

spots.name: Yokohama Chinatown
spots.blurb: The biggest Chinatown in Japan. Steam buns on every corner, the Kanteibyo temple at the center.

spots.name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
spots.blurb: The underground Showa streetscape of regional ramen shops. Half-portion bowls let you eat through the map. Five minutes on foot from Shin-Yokohama Station.

spots.name: Autobacs ASM Yokohama
spots.blurb: The legendary GT-R tuner shop. Car culture otaku territory, not anime, but the garage energy is the same.
spots.matched: 神奈川県横浜市保土ケ谷区川島町

spots.name: Fuji-Q Highland
spots.blurb: The coaster park at the mountain's foot. Eejanaika and Fujiyama are the headliners.

spots.name: NARUTO×BORUTO FUJI HIDDEN VILLAGE OF KONOHA
spots.blurb: The Hidden Leaf land inside Fuji-Q. Ichiraku ramen, shinobi missions, and Mount Fuji photobombing the Hokage monument.
spots.matched: NARUTO×BORUTO FUJI HIDDEN VILLAGE OF KONOHA

spots.name: Ghibli Park
spots.blurb: The Ghibli park on the old Expo grounds in Nagakute. Mostly walks through built worlds: the bakery from Kiki, Satsuki and Mei's house, the Grand Warehouse. The Valley of Witches has two rides, a carousel and the Castle in the Sky Flying Machine. Timed entry, plan ahead.
spots.matched: 愛知県長久手市茨ケ廻間乙１５３３番地

spots.name: Nipponbashi Denden Town
spots.blurb: Osaka's Akihabara, on Nipponbashi-suji. Animate, Super Potato, Jungle, figure shops, maid cafes, card shops. More local, less tourist-polished.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市浪速区日本橋四丁目１５番

spots.name: JOJOPUB
spots.blurb: A JoJo's Bizarre Adventure themed bar in Kyoto, a train ride up from Osaka. Stand-named cocktails.

spots.name: Eorzea Cafe Osaka
spots.blurb: The Osaka branch of the FFXIV cafe in Dotonbori's Pasela building. Same menu cycle, easier to book than Akihabara.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市中央区道頓堀一丁目４番２７号

spots.name: Good Smile x Animate Cafe Osaka
spots.blurb: The rotating-collab cafe in Nipponbashi. Whatever property is running that month gets the menu, the coasters, the whole room.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市浪速区日本橋四丁目１５番１７号

spots.name: Osaka Castle
spots.blurb: The castle on the hill that Godzilla wrecked in 1955. The park around it is Osaka's best skyline frame.

spots.name: The Landmark Square Osaka
spots.blurb: The restaurant complex in the old Osaka Castle park buildings. Good lunch stop after the castle keep.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市中央区大阪城３番１号

spots.name: Dotonbori
spots.blurb: The neon canal strip. The Glico runner, takoyaki on every corner, kushikatsu rules about double dipping enforced by signage.

spots.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
spots.blurb: Osaka's market street. Scallops grilled in the shell, wagyu skewers, fruit you cannot afford. Eat walking.

spots.name: National Bunraku Theatre
spots.blurb: The puppet theater near Nipponbashi. Three puppeteers work each puppet.

spots.name: Umeda Sky Building
spots.blurb: The floating garden observatory. The escalator through the sky is the shot.

spots.name: Takimikoji
spots.blurb: The retro Showa food street in the Sky Building basement. Cheap lunch in a film set.

spots.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
spots.blurb: The museum with a full-size Edo street indoors, sky effects overhead. Walk a 19th-century Osaka block in yukata.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市北区天神橋六丁目４番２０号

spots.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
spots.blurb: One of the world's great aquariums, built around a central Pacific tank with a whale shark. On the bay, pairs with the USJ side.

spots.name: teamLab Botanical Garden Osaka
spots.blurb: The night botanical garden in Nagai Park. Art projected onto real trees. Evening only.

spots.name: teamLab: Field of Wind, Rain and Sun
spots.blurb: The outdoor teamLab installation near Osaka's eastern edge. Weather itself becomes the medium.
spots.matched: teamLab: Field of Wind, Rain and Sun

spots.name: Osaka Expo 2025 site
spots.blurb: The Yumeshima site of Expo 2025, which closed in October 2025.
spots.matched: 大阪府大阪市此花区夢洲中一丁目

spots.name: Universal Studios Japan
spots.blurb: The park. Super Nintendo World alone justifies the day: the Mario Kart ride, Power-Up Band blocks, Kinopio's Cafe. Harry Potter, and rotating anime collabs (One Piece, Monster Hunter, Spy x Family). Buy Express Pass early or learn the single-rider lines.

spots.name: Hakutsuru Sake Brewery Museum
spots.blurb: The sake museum in Nada's brewery district. Old wooden tools, free tasting, the smell of fermentation doing half the teaching.

spots.name: Kobe Shushinkan
spots.blurb: The Fukuju brewery in Nada. The shop pours tastings under a cedar ball, the restaurant serves sake lees dishes.
spots.matched: 兵庫県神戸市東灘区住吉南町一丁目８番

spots.name: Nijigen no Mori
spots.blurb: The anime park inside Awaji's prefectural forest. Free entry to the grounds; each attraction zone tickets separately. This is the reason the island is on the route.
spots.matched: Naruto x Boruto park Nijigen no mori

spots.name: Naruto x Boruto park
spots.blurb: Shinobi zone in Nijigen no Mori. A real Hidden Leaf with the Hokage faces on the cliff, maze missions, and Ichiraku ramen at the exit.
spots.matched: Naruto x Boruto park Nijigen no mori

spots.name: Dragon Quest Island
spots.blurb: The outdoor Dragon Quest RPG zone. Walk a real map, fight slimes, level a party. Your name on a party roster.

spots.name: Godzilla Interception Operation
spots.blurb: Zipline into the mouth of a life-size Godzilla bust erupting from the ground. Absurd, magnificent, the island's best headline.

spots.name: Godzilla Museum
spots.blurb: The museum beside the zipline. Suits, props, storyboards, seventy years of the King in one hall.

spots.name: Hello Kitty Smile
spots.blurb: The Kitty palace on the west coast. Gallery rooms, projection mapping, a restaurant facing the strait.

spots.name: Hello Kitty Show Box
spots.blurb: The Kitty show restaurant up the road. Lunch service with a stage show. The roof is a giant Kitty face visible from the air.
spots.matched: 兵庫県淡路市野島平林

spots.name: Awajishima Onion Kitchen
spots.blurb: The burger stand at Uzunooka by the Naruto bridge. Awaji onions on everything, including the onion rings the size of bracelets.
spots.matched: 兵庫県南あわじ市福良乙

spots.name: Greenarium Awajishima
spots.blurb: A strawberry-picking farm with a restaurant, cafe and barbecue.
spots.matched: 兵庫県淡路市野島常盤

spots.name: miele the DINER
spots.blurb: The seaside diner by Hello Kitty Smile. Awaji burgers and shakes on the terrace over the water.

spots.name: 168 Gelato Caffe
spots.blurb: Gelato in the Nijigen no Mori corner of the island. Cold sugar after the zipline.

spots.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
spots.blurb: Off the island over the second-longest suspension span in the world. Maiko station sits under the bridge deck; the glass-floor promenade is worth twenty minutes.

spots.name: Kobe Airport
spots.blurb: The airport on its own island in the harbor, eighteen minutes from Sannomiya on the Port Liner. This is the hop home.

spots.name: Haneda Airport
spots.blurb: Land at Haneda, not Narita: thirty minutes from the city. The bags are already at the hotel because you couriered them from Awaji.

spots.name: Akihabara, again
spots.blurb: The buy list gets executed. The figure you passed on at Tamashii, the retro cart at Super Potato, the find at Radio Kaikan. Second pass through the district with a list and a budget.

spots.name: Nakano Broadway, one more pass
spots.blurb: The grail check. Broadway is where the thing you could not find in Akihabara is sitting in a glass case.

spots.name: Tokyo Character Street, the omiyage run
spots.blurb: Last stop before the airport. About thirty character shops in one underground strip, so the gift pile takes forty minutes.

spots.name: Phone Booth (Kanda Catholic Church)
spots.blurb: Fans match this Jinbocho phone booth to the one where Reze runs in out of the rain and meets Denji, who coughs up a flower he had eaten and gives it to her. Guides note that no real booth matches the film exactly.

spots.name: Aoi Building
spots.blurb: The Aoi Building on Hakusan-dori appears in the background as Reze walks to her part-time job at the café.

spots.name: Onnazaka (Women's Slope)
spots.blurb: Fans say the slope where Denji and Reze walk together in the film is based on Onnazaka, a stone stairway between Jinbocho and Ochanomizu. Visitors have left gerbera flowers on the landing.

spots.name: Trois Bagues Vertes (Café Futamichi)
spots.blurb: Fans identify Trois Bagues Vertes near Jinbocho Station as the model for the café where Reze works, though this has not been officially confirmed. At the end of the film, Denji waits there with flowers for Reze, who never arrives, and Power shows up and fights with him over the bouquet.

spots.name: Nerima Station South Exit
spots.blurb: In episode 2, on Denji's first patrol with Power, a call requests backup in front of Nerima Station for the Sea Cucumber Devil. Power leaps from a building and kills it with a hammer made of blood, claiming the kill as hers.

spots.name: Shibuya Station — Hachiko Exit
spots.blurb: On October 31 a curtain falls over Shibuya, trapping civilians so that Gojo cannot freely use his domain. Just outside this exit, at the Scramble Crossing, Megumi fights his father, Toji, in episode 40.

spots.name: Shibuya Station — Underground B5F
spots.blurb: On the Fukutoshin Line platform at B5F, Kenjaku opens the Prison Realm, and Gojo is stunned at the sight of Geto's body. In the one minute that passes in his mind, the seal completes and Gojo is sealed.

spots.name: Shibuya Hikarie
spots.blurb: Gojo arrives at Shibuya Hikarie B3F in episode 32 and sees the crowd trapped inside the barrier. Below it, inside the Hikarie 1 gate of the Tokyo Metro station, Yuji fights Choso, who stops short of killing him after seeing false memories of Yuji as his brother.

spots.name: Shibuya Mark City
spots.blurb: The Mark City connecting walkway, with Okamoto Taro's mural, is matched to episode 38, where Naobito Zenin, Maki and Nanami face Dagon.

spots.name: Harajuku Station
spots.blurb: In episode 3, Yuji and Megumi sit outside Harajuku Station waiting for Gojo, who comes down from the station and waves. The group then meets Nobara by the coin lockers near Takeshita Street.

spots.name: Roppongi Hills
spots.blurb: After meeting at Harajuku, Gojo takes the first-years to Roppongi, where Nobara fights curses with her hammer and nails. In the first opening, Nobara appears in a shot that guides place beside Roppongi Hills.

spots.name: Sendagaya Tunnel
spots.blurb: Sendagaya Tunnel is the setting for Megumi's shot in the first opening sequence.

spots.name: Otaguro Park (Suginami)
spots.blurb: In the first opening, Maki appears in Otaguro Park wearing the glasses she uses to see cursed spirits, with a curse rising from the pond.

spots.name: Kichijoji Kinema Cinema
spots.blurb: Guides identify Kichijoji Plaza, which has a rooftop batting center, as the model for the Kinema Cinema. There Junpei watches Mahito kill three boys who had bullied him and follows him out, and Mahito later draws him into his hideout and manipulates him.

spots.name: Shinjuku Café (Geto meeting)
spots.blurb: Geto crosses a Shinjuku street with the cursed spirits Jogo and Hanami, a crossing guides place at Kabukicho Intersection. At a nearby restaurant, Jogo proposes killing Gojo in exchange for the Prison Realm, and the heat around him kills the people inside.

spots.name: Nanami's Former Office (Shinjuku)
spots.blurb: After graduating from Jujutsu High, Nanami left sorcery for an office job before returning to work as a sorcerer. A pilgrimage guide places his old office in Shinjuku but does not name the building.

spots.name: Museum Café (Model for :re)
spots.blurb: Museum Cafe and Diner, a few minutes from Kanamecho Station, is reported as the real model for :re, the coffee shop Touka runs. In episode 2 of :re, Haise stops in and cries after tasting her coffee.

spots.name: Milky Way Café (Ikebukuro)
spots.blurb: In episode 1, Kaneki and Rize have lunch at the Milky Way café in Ikebukuro during their date.

spots.name: Wako Namiki-Dori Building (Godzilla Minus One)
spots.blurb: The Ginza clock tower that Godzilla takes down in Minus One. Still standing. The intersection below is the film's ground zero.

spots.name: Nakagin Capsule Tower site
spots.blurb: Kurokawa's capsule tower was demolished in 2022. Some capsules survive in museums.

spots.name: Godzilla Square
spots.blurb: The Godzilla statue in Hibiya Chanter Square, successor to the old one from 1995. He guards the cinema district that made him.

spots.name: National Diet Building (Shin Godzilla)
spots.blurb: In Shin Godzilla the government works out of the Prime Minister's residence nearby, and the Diet Building is shown burning after Godzilla's atomic breath.

spots.name: DevilCraft Kanda
spots.blurb: Chicago deep dish and craft beer in Kanda. A good recovery spot after an Akihabara day.

spots.name: Godzilla Head
spots.blurb: The full-size Godzilla head looming over the Toho Building in Kabukicho. It roars on the hour with light and smoke.

spots.name: Godzilla Store Tokyo
spots.blurb: The official kaiju merchandise store on the first floor of the Shinjuku Marui Annex, near the Godzilla head.

spots.name: Square Enix Co., Ltd.
spots.blurb: The headquarters in Shinjuku Eastside Square. The Square Enix Cafe and shop opened in 2026 in the Pasela Tower near Shinjuku Station.

spots.name: Tokyo Tower
spots.blurb: The 1958 orange tower. Godzilla damages it in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah and Godzilla: Tokyo SOS, and other monsters, Mothra among them, have wrecked it too. The view is still the romantic one.

spots.name: Suga Shrine Stairs (Your Name)
spots.blurb: The staircase to Suga Shrine in Yotsuya is where Taki and Mitsuha finally meet in person at the end of Your Name. It also appears on the film's posters.

spots.name: Shinanomachi Station Footbridge (Your Name)
spots.blurb: After his date with Okudera, Taki crosses this footbridge by Shinanomachi Station and tries to call Mitsuha.

spots.name: Shintoshin Footbridge (Your Name)
spots.blurb: Guides identify the Shintoshin footbridge in Nishi-Shinjuku as the place where Taki and Mitsuha cross paths one night without realizing it.

spots.name: Cafe La Boheme Shinjuku Gyoen (Your Name)
spots.blurb: Cafe La Boheme, facing Shinjuku Gyoen, is the model for Il Giardino delle Parole, the Italian restaurant where Taki and Okudera work.
spots.matched: Cafe La Boheme Shinjuku Gyoen (Your Name)

spots.name: National Art Center Tokyo (Your Name)
spots.blurb: Taki and Okudera have lunch on their date at Salon de Thé Rond, the café inside the National Art Center.

spots.name: Hijiri Bridge and Ochanomizu Station (Suzume)
spots.blurb: The tracks, brick walls and slopes around the Hijiribashi exit of Ochanomizu Station appear almost exactly as they are in real life when Suzume rushes there searching for Souta.

spots.name: Aoyama Cemetery (JJK)
spots.blurb: Gojo mentions Aoyama Cemetery in episode 3 of Jujutsu Kaisen, and during the Shibuya Incident it is the meeting point for Mei Mei's group.

spots.name: Rikkyo University (Tokyo Ghoul)
spots.blurb: The 2017 live-action film Tokyo Ghoul shot its Kamii University scenes at Rikkyo University's Ikebukuro campus.

spots.name: Takazawa Bridge and Kenryuji (Tsuki ga Kirei)
spots.blurb: The view of Takazawa Bridge with Kenryuji beside it is part of the establishing shots of Kawagoe in the opening minute of Tsuki ga Kirei.
spots.matched: Takazawa Bridge and Kenryuji (Tsuki ga Kirei)

spots.name: Kawagoe Matsuecho Post Office (Tsuki ga Kirei)
spots.blurb: Kotaro mails something at this post office about sixteen minutes into the first episode of Tsuki ga Kirei.
spots.matched: Kawagoe Matsuecho Post Office (Tsuki ga Kirei)

spots.name: NTV Big Clock
spots.blurb: The giant mechanical clock Hayao Miyazaki designed for Nittele Tower in Shiodome, unveiled in 2006. It runs a three-minute show at 12:00, 15:00, 18:00 and 20:00, with a 10:00 show on weekends.

spots.name: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum
spots.blurb: Historic buildings moved to a park in Koganei. Its Takei Sanshodo stationery shop is cited by Ghibli as a source for the drawer wall in Kamaji's boiler room in Spirited Away.

spots.name: Shirohige’s Cream Puff Factory
spots.blurb: The bakery in Daita, Setagaya, known for Totoro-shaped cream puffs. It is run by Hayao Miyazaki's nephew.

spots.name: Toho Studios Godzilla Statue
spots.blurb: The Godzilla statue at the entrance to Toho Studios in Seijo, beside a Seven Samurai mural.

spots.name: Sakurai Japanese Tea Experience
spots.blurb: A tea room on the fifth floor of the Spiral building in Minami-Aoyama, run by tea master Shinya Sakurai. The course serves gyokuro over three infusions, the last as an iced cocktail with shiso and lime.

spots.name: Yakumo Saryo
spots.blurb: Shinichiro Ogata's tea house in a former Japanese home overlooking a garden in Meguro. The Asacha tea breakfast starts at 9:00 and needs a reservation; no children under 15 at breakfast. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

spots.name: Suzukien Asakusa
spots.blurb: Matcha gelato in seven strengths, from Suzukien tea shop and the Shizuoka matcha-sweets maker Nanaya. No. 7 is billed as the strongest in the world.

spots.name: Cafe de l'Ambre
spots.blurb: A Ginza coffee house open since 1948, with more than thirty single origins, many of them aged for years.

spots.name: Old House Cafe Rengetsu
spots.blurb: A 1933 building in Ikegami that was long a soba shop with an inn upstairs. The old menus, counter and wall safe are still there.

spots.name: LATTE ART MANIA TOKYO
spots.blurb: A small coffee bar in Kita-Aoyama, near Gaienmae Station, run by a four-time latte art champion. The signature is a black latte colored with bamboo charcoal.

spots.name: COFFEE JAZZ GENIUS
spots.blurb: A jazz kissa founded in Shibuya in 1970 and in Nakano since 1989, three minutes from Nakano-Shimbashi Station. About 8,000 records and a Vitavox speaker built into the wall. Closed Thursdays.

spots.name: Fruits Parlor Goto
spots.blurb: An Asakusa fruit parlor founded in 1946. The parfait of the day uses seven fruits, and the menu changes with the season. Closed Wednesdays.

spots.name: Benitsuru
spots.blurb: Rice-flour pancakes cooked on a copper griddle, near Tawaramachi. Limited numbers each day; reservations online.

spots.name: HIGUMA Doughnuts Tokyo Dome City
spots.blurb: Freshly fried doughnuts made with Hokkaido ingredients, in the Tokyo Dome City attractions area.

spots.name: Vampire Cafe
spots.blurb: A Dracula-themed restaurant on the seventh floor of a Ginza building, open since 2001: red velvet, chandeliers and a coffin.

spots.name: ART AQUARIUM MUSEUM GINZA
spots.blurb: About 5,000 goldfish shown with traditional crafts such as Edo kiriko glass, in the Ginza Mitsukoshi annex.

spots.name: Gotokuji Temple
spots.blurb: The lucky-cat temple in Setagaya, five minutes from Miyanosaka Station. More than a thousand donated maneki-neko fill the grounds, which are free and open 6:00 to 17:00.

spots.name: KEY’S CAFE Akihabara
spots.blurb: Specialty coffee under the tracks between Akihabara and Okachimachi, open from 7:00. Wifi and room for a group.

spots.name: Gallery and Coffee Shop Utsuwa
spots.blurb: A cafe and gallery in a Western-style house in Gotemba. Open Monday and Thursday to Saturday, 11:00 to 14:00.

spots.name: Saijoen and the Matcha Museum
spots.blurb: Aiya's tea house and garden in Nishio, the matcha town south of Nagoya. The Matcha Museum next door runs a 75-minute guided course by reservation, with blending, grinding your own matcha and a short tea ceremony.

spots.name: MACCHA HOUSE Kyoto Kawaramachi
spots.blurb: Matcha tiramisu two minutes from Hankyu Kawaramachi Station in Kyoto.

spots.name: ROKUYOSHA
spots.blurb: A Kyoto coffee house founded in 1950 near Kawaramachi-Sanjo, with a bar in the basement since 1969. The homemade doughnuts are the signature.

spots.name: Masahiko Ozumi Paris
spots.blurb: Osaka pastry shop known for the Zabuton Mont Blanc, a cushion of chestnut strands.

spots.name: Rikuro’s Namba Main Branch
spots.blurb: Jiggly Osaka cheesecake, lighter and eggier than the dense Western style, with raisins on the bottom.

spots.name: Kashihara Street Fighter Statues
spots.blurb: Kashihara in Nara is the hometown of Capcom's founder. Bronze statues of Ryu, Chun-Li, Ken and E. Honda, Street Fighter manhole covers and a mural stand around Kintetsu Yamato-Yagi Station.
